issue_context.title: controller_util_test.go does not follow similar patterns as other unit tests in the repo.
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

During implementation of KEP 3393 (PodReplacementPolicy for Jobs) we found that the unit tests of [controller_util_test.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/controller_utils_test.go) do not follow common patterns established in k/k.  

1) The tests are not written using table driven design (https://dave.cheney.net/2019/05/07/prefer-table-driven-tests).

2) The tests use `Differences` rather than `Cmp.Diff`.

This probably should be done as two separate PRs but wanted to highlight some areas that could use some cleanup. 

### Why is this needed?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117015#discussion_r1254470573

Not using `Cmp.Diff` means that we don't see diffs in the unit tests that makes this difficult.  

And not using table driven tests makes it difficult to add new test cases as it usually is brought up during review that we should use a table-driven test but the entire file does not obey this format.

review_comments: I'm wondering if we could wrap the entire scenario into table based tests. The parameters could include the: 10 adds and 30 deletes as parameters. For example: `initialExpectationsForAdditions`, `initialExpectationsForDeletions`, then `observedAdditions`, `observedDeletions`. Then to verify maybe `wantExpectationsForAdditions` and `wantExpectationsForDeletions`.

I can see changes to the test case applied and they look good, but I think we can still to better.

Currently it is not clear what the test is focused on, and what are the actions we are testing. For example, it has non-obvious asserts in the preparatory phase: `assert.False(t, e.SatisfiedExpectations(logger, rcKey), "Rc will sync before expectations are met")`. 

More concrete proposal to structure the test:  
 1.  setup expectations, seems just `SetExpectations` based on `expectationsToSet` (or renamed to `initialExpectations`)
 2. perform actions , represented as `CreationObserved`, `DeletionObserved`, and expiring by clock shift; based on `creationsObserved`, `deletionsObserved` and `expireExpectations`
 3. asserts: verify results of `GetExpectations` and `SatisfiedExpectations`
  
 Then, all the test code (except potentially some consts definitions) could be inside `t.Run`. 
 
 Still, I think the test looks already better than it was, so I'm ok with accepting it as is, and doing the improvements in a follow up.

I find this test setup to be a bit confusing.  

Is it possible to inline the testcases with the functions rather than a nested functions?

I usually like to see a list of the test cases defined and their functions and then the test case just run thoses.  

Seeing these nested functions confuses me a bit.

I did it this way because of the [second test case](https://github.com/kaisoz/kubernetes/blob/02aca97542f83229b15b7b1e1c4aeb017e7e7172/pkg/controller/controller_utils_test.go#L362). As you can see, the `generateName` variable is used both in the `podCreationFunc` function and the `expectedPod` substruct.

The main problem is that, in Golang you can't reference a struct member from another struct member at struct definition time. So if I added the `generateName` variable to the test struct declaration, I'd get a compilation error when referencing it from both the `podCreationFunc` function and the `expectedPod` substruct.

I could define the `generateName` variable outside of the test array definition but that feels uncoherent because it's test input data and not logic.

Another solution would be to split the function again (which would make sense) and have one for testing the pod creation, and another to test the pod creation with name.

Does this make sense? WDYT?
I’ve seen many examples of defining constants out of test cases and using those in struct defining.  I think that’s a good way to approach it.  A separate function seems heavy handed imo.
ok then! so I'll do it that way 👍🏻 . I proposed a different function because this function used to be two in the previous version

IIUC `name` and `numReplicas` fully characterize each test case. Thus, could drop `rcKey` and `rcPodNames` from test parameters and then inline `prepareTests` inside `t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {`?
